issues.legal_issue: Co-widows who inherit an estate jointly with survivorship rights may, by mutual arrangement accompanying a partition, relinquish survivorship rights in the property allotted to the other.
material_facts: Two widows inherited their husband's property as joint tenants with rights of survivorship and equal beneficial enjoyment.
The widows divided most of the property and separately possessed and enjoyed their allotted portions.
The dispute raised whether they were legally capable of agreeing that each would relinquish survivorship rights in the property allotted to the other.
issues.conclusion: The widows were competent to partition the property and, as part of that arrangement, to agree to relinquish survivorship rights in the property allotted to the other. Such an arrangement was not prohibited by section 6(a) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hindu law, co-widows inheriting property with rights of survivorship could partition it for separate possession. Although neither could unilaterally compel an absolute partition destroying survivorship, they could do so by mutual consent. A widow's present interest in inherited property, together with its incidental survivorship right, could be transferred; section 6(a) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 prohibits transfer of the bare chance of succeeding to the entire estate, not transfer of that present interest with its incidental right. The Court relied on Bhugwan Deen Doobey v. Myna Baee, Gauri Nath Kakaji v. Gaya Kuar, Commissioner of Income-tax v. Smt. Indira Balakrishna, Ramakkal v. Ramasami Naickan, and Sudalai Ammal v. Gomathi Ammal; it also referred to analogous decisions concerning daughters inheriting jointly.

predicates.co_widows_inherit_with_survivorship: Two widows inherit an estate jointly with rights of survivorship.
predicates.co_widows_mutually_agree_to_partition: The co-widows mutually agree to divide the inherited property into separate holdings.
predicates.agreement_covers_survivorship_rights: The parties' agreement addresses relinquishment of survivorship rights in the holdings allotted to each other.

issues.definition: When co-widows inherit jointly with survivorship rights and mutually agree to partition the property on terms covering those rights, their agreement may validly relinquish survivorship rights in the other widow's allotted property.

issues.legal_issue: A new objection to partition documents cannot be raised for the first time on appeal when deciding it would require further factual investigation.
material_facts: At trial, the case proceeded on the basis that the partition was oral and that the written partition lists were evidence of that oral partition.
No objection to the admissibility of the partition lists was raised at trial.
The objection that the lists required registration was raised for the first time in the High Court appeal.
Resolving that objection would have required further investigation of factual questions.
issues.conclusion: The High Court correctly declined to entertain the new registration objection for the first time on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: An oral partition is possible, and written lists may serve as evidence of an oral partition and an associated oral agreement. A new objection raised for the first time on appeal need not be entertained where its determination requires further factual investigation.

predicates.appeal_from_trial_decision: The matter is an appeal from a trial decision.
predicates.objection_first_raised_on_appeal: A party raises the objection for the first time in the appellate court.
predicates.deciding_objection_requires_further_fact: Resolving the objection would require further investigation of factual questions.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a trial decision, a new objection requiring further factual investigation is not entertained when first raised on appeal.

issues.legal_issue: Partition and separate enjoyment alone do not extinguish co-widows' survivorship rights, and the party asserting an agreement to relinquish those rights must prove it by clear and cogent evidence.
material_facts: The co-widows divided the property, took separate possession, and separately enjoyed their allotted portions.
The partition lists said that each widow would take and enjoy her allotted property but contained no words expressly indicating relinquishment of survivorship rights.
Other evidence, including the continued joint names on land records and the parties' dealings with some properties, did not clearly establish an agreement to relinquish those rights.
The trial court rejected the evidence offered to establish an oral agreement to relinquish survivorship rights, and the Supreme Court found that conclusion correct.
issues.conclusion: The respondent failed to prove by clear and cogent evidence that the widows agreed to relinquish survivorship rights. The partition did not itself destroy those rights, and the High Court erred in finding otherwise; the appeal was allowed and the trial court's decree restored.
issues.legal_principle: Mere partition of an estate between co-widows does not destroy each widow's right of survivorship in property allotted to the other. The party asserting an arrangement relinquishing survivorship must establish it by clear and cogent evidence. The Court found the partition lists and other evidence insufficient to meet that burden.

predicates.co_widows_partition_estate: Co-widows divide an inherited estate and separately possess or enjoy their allotted portions.
predicates.party_asserts_survivorship_relinquishmen: A party relies on an alleged agreement by the co-widows to relinquish survivorship rights in each other's allotted property.
predicates.evidence_does_not_clearly_establish_reli: The evidence does not clearly and cogently establish that the co-widows agreed to relinquish those rights.

issues.definition: When co-widows partition and separately enjoy an estate, a party asserting that they relinquished survivorship rights must prove that agreement with clear and cogent evidence; partition alone does not establish relinquishment.
